title: Getting comfortable with manufacturing
original_goal: I want to get comfortable with manufacturing!

question_selection.note: The first task is to collaboratively choose meaningful questions, not to presume a single manufacturing curriculum.

candidate_parent_purposes.purpose: Understand the landscape of processes and what each makes possible
candidate_parent_purposes.distinguishing_probe: Can I recognize plausible production methods for unfamiliar objects?

candidate_parent_purposes.purpose: Develop practical ability to design and make functioning things
candidate_parent_purposes.distinguishing_probe: Can I go from requirements and drawings to a working part or assembly?

candidate_parent_purposes.purpose: Understand manufacturing as an industrial production system
candidate_parent_purposes.distinguishing_probe: Can I reason about yield, tolerances, tooling, quality, throughput, supply chain, and economics?

candidate_parent_purposes.purpose: Understand the physics and limitations of material transformation
candidate_parent_purposes.distinguishing_probe: Can I explain why a process works, where it fails, and what could extend its limits?

question_selection.selected_by_user: Explore the whole manufacturing landscape; Learn to actually make things

entry_questions.question: How was this object manufactured?
entry_questions.information_gain: Learn process recognition and industrial inference

entry_questions.question: How many different ways could we manufacture this object?
entry_questions.information_gain: Map process alternatives and discriminating constraints

entry_questions.question: What would prevent us from manufacturing this object ourselves?
entry_questions.information_gain: Identify actionable missing capabilities and economical substitutes

question_selection.next_collaborative_choice: Clarify whether the most exciting shared question is (a) understanding possible artifacts/physical transformations, (b) maximizing individual manufacturing agency, or (c) the growth and bootstrapping of manufacturing ecosystems; multiple can remain active. Do not select an object or curriculum.

selected_big_picture_questions.verbatim: How could I learn to make almost anything?
How do capabilities compose and bootstrap?

question_selection.user_direction: Investigate the relationships among these parent questions, alternative formulations, and what pursuing each could reveal. Do not choose an object or reading curriculum yet.
question_selection.candidate_parent: How can we understand, navigate, acquire, and expand humanity's capacity to make physical things?
distinctions: Feasible in physical principle vs demonstrated by human industry vs accessible to an individual
One-off artifact vs reliable repeated production
Owning a process vs accessing it through services, institutions or collaborators
Having capabilities vs knowing which compositions are possible and what dependencies block them

alternative_formulations.question: What physical structures and properties can we create?
What cannot we manufacture, and which limits are fundamental versus contingent?
How did the present manufacturing frontier arise?
What capabilities would give me the greatest manufacturing reach?
alternative_formulations.why: Optimizes generative competence rather than a tool checklist

alternative_formulations.question: What can I accomplish through accessible external manufacturing?
What would operational confidence on unfamiliar manufacturing tasks look like?
Which initial capability sets can generate or unlock others?
Which capabilities are bottlenecks, bridges, or multiplicative complements?
Under what conditions can a production system reproduce or improve its own tooling?
alternative_formulations.why: Investigates closure, dependency and external inputs

cross_relations.relation: Human production capabilities delimit accessible learning opportunities but do not determine which are worth acquiring
Capability acquisition can increase ability to acquire or create further capabilities
Bootstrapping and composition can expand the frontier of actually manufacturable outcomes

proposed_root_question: How can we understand and acquire the capabilities needed to manufacture an increasingly broad variety of physical things?
